title: Garden Steps
statement: A garden path has n stepping stones. You can step to the next stone or skip one. Count the different ways to cross a path of up to 80 stones.

approaches.name: Loop from the start, keeping only the last two counts
approaches.label: best
approaches.why: Each count is the sum of the two before it, so two variables are enough.

approaches.name: Recursion that remembers each result
approaches.label: valid
approaches.why: Correct and fast, but it keeps a table and a call stack of size n.

approaches.name: Plain recursion without remembering
approaches.hint: Call the function on both smaller cases
approaches.label: valid
approaches.why: Correct, but it recomputes the same counts so often that 80 stones would take ages.

approaches.name: Double the count for every stone
approaches.label: unsuitable
approaches.why: Skipping is not free at every stone: 3 stones have 3 ways, not 8.

title: Signal Boost
statement: A signal is multiplied by the same gain g, k times, and you need the result modulo 1,000,000,007. k can be up to 10^18.

approaches.name: Square the result for k / 2, multiply by g once more if k is odd
approaches.label: best
approaches.why: The exponent halves every call, so about 60 calls cover 10^18.

approaches.name: Multiply by g, k times
approaches.hint: Do exactly what the statement says
approaches.label: valid
approaches.why: Correct, but 10^18 multiplications would never finish.

approaches.name: Use the language's floating-point power and then take the remainder
approaches.label: unsuitable
approaches.why: The exact number is far too big; floating point loses the digits, so the remainder is wrong.

title: Shuffle Score
statement: A game scores how shuffled a deck of up to 200,000 numbered cards is: the number of pairs where a higher card comes before a lower one.

approaches.name: Count while merge sorting
approaches.hint: Split, solve the halves, count across them while combining
approaches.label: best
approaches.why: Pairs inside each half are counted recursively; pairs across the halves are counted during the merge.

approaches.name: Check every pair with two loops
approaches.hint: Compare each card with all later cards
approaches.label: valid
approaches.why: Correct, but 200,000 cards means about 20 billion comparisons.

approaches.name: Sort the deck and count cards that moved
approaches.label: unsuitable
approaches.why: How many cards moved is not the number of out-of-order pairs: 3 1 2 has 3 moved cards but 2 pairs.
